newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Heavy rains in Oklahoma, Texas.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Heavy rains in Oklahoma, Texas.

text.p: Heavy rains were falling Thursday in Oklahoma and Texas, but grain merchandisers said the showers would likely miss the Panhandle growing areas of those states.
"We've gotten about a 1/4 inch and there's more to come. We need it bad -- we haven't had measurable moisture since just after Christmas," a north central Oklahoma dealer said.
The dealer said southwest Oklahoma was supposed to receive one to two inches of rain by Friday.
A dealer in Wichita, Kansas, said the rains were moving northeast and would miss the western half of his state.
"It's overcast and we're only supposed to get 1/10 of an inch or less. It's all falling to the southeast of us," the Kansas dealer said.
Another dealer said western Kansas will likely see high winds Thursday, raising the possibility of unwanted soil movement.
Meanwhile, basis bids for hard red winter wheat were mixed Thursday, and grain dealers in Kansas said that while wheat sales were slow, sales of new crop corn were brisk.
"The farmer's got to be thinking that now is the time to sell his corn," a central Kansas dealer said.
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
(Note: H=KCBT March wheat futures. K=KCBT May wheat futures.
